statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-62898 (GHSA-c494-m2fq-59mx) is a use-after-free in Microsoft QUIC (MsQuic) as used by .NET that lets an attacker disclose information over a network. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and, for .NET 10, only the Windows runtime packs (Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64), affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.10 and fixed in 10.0.11 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c494-m2fq-59mx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/426, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.11/10.0.11.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: no file in them has msquic in its name and no ELF file in them lists an MsQuic library as a dependency, so none contains an MsQuic library. Every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly with a CLR header; none is a native Windows executable or DLL, so no Windows runtime pack is present.

CVE-2026-62898 (GHSA-c494-m2fq-59mx) is an information disclosure issue in Microsoft QUIC (MsQuic): a use after free lets an attacker disclose information over a network. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the .NET 8.0 runtime packs for Windows (win-x64, win-x86, win-arm64), which bundle the MsQuic library, as the affected packages, fixed in 8.0.30 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c494-m2fq-59mx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/426, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.30/8.0.30.md, and the upstream discussion at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/132154). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux (linux-musl) from Microsoft's source release. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. No MsQuic library is present: no file named msquic.dll or libmsquic.so, in any form, is in any of the packages. They carry the managed System.Net.Quic assembly, which on Linux uses a libmsquic library only if one is installed separately on the system, and no Windows runtime pack. None of the packages contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file (every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly). So the vulnerable MsQuic code is not in this owner.
